name: vgic_v2_populate_lr
prose: Function taking vcpu, an irq and an LR index lr; the caller must hold irq->irq_lock (stated in the comment above it) and lr must be a valid index of vcpu->arch.vgic_cpu.vgic_v2.vgic_lr. It builds val starting from irq->intid and then: if irq->active, sets the active bit, for an SGI also puts irq->active_source into the source-CPU field, and for a multi-source SGI sets the EOI bit and forbids the pending bit; sets the group-1 bit if irq->group; if irq->hw and the IRQ does not need resampling it sets the HW bit and puts irq->hwintid in the physical-ID field, and forbids the pending bit when the IRQ is active; otherwise (not HW, or HW needing resampling) it sets the EOI bit if irq->config is VGIC_CONFIG_LEVEL and, for an active level IRQ, forbids the pending bit. Hence a mapped HW level IRQ that needs no resampling does not get the EOI bit from this step. If the pending bit is allowed and irq_is_pending(irq): it sets the pending bit; for an edge IRQ it clears irq->pending_latch; for an SGI it takes src = ffs(irq->source) and, if src is 0, emits a rate-limited warning and returns without writing vgic_lr[lr] (pending_latch of an edge IRQ has already been cleared at that point), otherwise puts src - 1 in the source-CPU field, clears that bit of irq->source and, if other source bits remain, sets irq->pending_latch again and sets the EOI bit. If the IRQ is a mapped level IRQ and the pending bit was set it clears irq->line_level. It then ORs in (irq->priority >> 3) at the priority position and stores val into vgic_lr[lr]. The only other return is the early one above; there is no error value.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: EOI is set for a level IRQ only in the non-HW-or-resampled branch (vgic-v2.c slice 150-153), so mapped HW level IRQs without resampling get none; old prose wrong. Round 2 (pending_latch re-set when sources remain) already stated in old prose and kept. Original (early return leaves lr unwritten) already stated. Slice 122-198.

name: early_pgtable_alloc
prose: Static __init function taking a page-table type argument that it does not use; it is for early boot allocation of a page-table page. It calls memblock_phys_alloc_range(PAGE_SIZE, PAGE_SIZE, 0, MEMBLOCK_ALLOC_NOLEAKTRACE) for one page. If that returns 0 it calls panic("Failed to allocate page table page"). Otherwise it returns the physical address that memblock returned (non-zero; the allocation was requested with PAGE_SIZE alignment). The page is not zeroed or otherwise written by this function. The only return is the final return phys.
note: Contract cleared: it depends on memblock global state (reviewers rounds 2 and 15 both complained about the contract). Panic path relies on panic() not returning. Slice lines 115-125.

name: note_page
prose: Callback of the arm64 page-table dumper taking the ptdump_state pointer pt_st, the start address addr of the next entry, its level and its raw entry value val; it returns nothing and takes no lock. The state st is the containing struct ptdump_pg_state (it must be initialised, with st->level == -1 meaning no range has been started yet; st->marker must have a valid element [1] to compare against; st->seq is passed unchanged to the print helpers, which are called whether or not it is NULL). Steps: if st->mm is set and (level == 1 and mm_p4d_folded(st->mm)) or (level == 2 and mm_pud_folded(st->mm)), level is changed to 0. prot is val & pg_level[level].mask when level >= 0 and 0 when level is negative (negative level, for example the -1 used to flush the last range, is allowed and does not index pg_level for the new entry). Then: (a) if st->level == -1 it records level, prot and addr as the current range and prints the header "---[ <marker name> ]---" for the current marker; (b) otherwise, if prot != st->current_prot, level != st->level or addr >= st->marker[1].start_address, it closes the current range: if st->current_prot is non-zero it calls note_prot_uxn and note_prot_wx (each does nothing unless st->check_wx is set; they may emit a one-time warning and add (addr - st->start_address) / PAGE_SIZE to st->uxn_pages or st->wx_pages when the old protection lacks UXN, or is not read-only and not PXN respectively); it prints the range start-addr, its size in K/M/G/T/P/E units and the name of pg_level[st->level], plus the protection bit names when st->current_prot is non-zero and that level has bits, then a newline; if addr >= st->marker[1].start_address it advances st->marker by one and prints the new marker header; finally it records addr, prot and level as the new current range; (c) if neither branch applies nothing is recorded. After (a), (b) or (c), if addr >= st->marker[1].start_address (re-evaluated) it advances st->marker by one more and prints the new marker header. So st->marker is advanced at most twice per call (at most once in cases (a) and (c)), even if addr lies beyond several marker boundaries.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: level < 0 is accepted (prot = 0, ptdump.c:204-205), so old precondition level >= 0 was wrong. Rounds 1 and 2 (marker advances at most twice per call, not for every boundary) already reflected in old prose and kept. note_prot_uxn/wx read at ptdump.c:160-189. Slice cut the head (function begins at slice line 191).

name: bpf_arch_text_poke
prose: Function bpf_arch_text_poke(ip, poke_type, old_addr, new_addr) that replaces the branch (or NOP) at ip that targets old_addr by one that targets new_addr (a NULL address means a NOP). Flow and returns: (1) if bpf_address_lookup(ip) fails it returns -ENOTSUPP (only bpf text can be poked); (2) offset == 0 means ip is the bpf prog entry: then plt is set to image + size - PLT_TARGET_OFFSET and ip is moved to the NOP slot at image + POKE_OFFSET instructions; (3) if either target is a long jump (more than 128MB from ip, NULL not counted) and ip is not the prog entry it WARNs and returns -EINVAL; (4) the branch type is link for BPF_MOD_CALL and non-link for any other poke_type; (5) it generates the old and new instructions with gen_branch_or_nop (a long jump is routed through plt) and returns -EFAULT if either generation fails; (6) plt_target is new_addr if the new target is a long jump, else &dummy_tramp if the old target is a long jump, else stays 0; only if plt_target is non-zero it makes the plt page writable (returning -EFAULT if set_memory_rw fails), writes plt->target with WRITE_ONCE and sets the page read-only again; this plt update happens before the instruction comparison below, so it can occur even when the function then returns 0 without patching; (7) if old_insn == new_insn it returns 0 without patching; (8) it takes text_mutex, reads the instruction at ip with aarch64_insn_read (any failure gives ret = -EFAULT), sets ret = -EFAULT if it differs from old_insn, otherwise ret = aarch64_insn_patch_text_nosync(ip, new_insn), then releases text_mutex and returns ret. text_mutex is held only in step (8) and released on both of its exits.
note: Reviewer round 15 right on both points: the plt may be rewritten before the old_insn == new_insn early return (bpf_jit_comp.c slice 51-71), and the plt write is only done when plt_target is non-zero (a long jump is involved), not for every bpf prog. Slice cut the head; name and locals read at bpf_jit_comp.c:2934-2956. is_long_jump/gen_branch_or_nop read at 2834-2863.

name: build_prologue
prose: Static function build_prologue(ctx, ebpf_from_cbpf) that emits the JIT prologue into ctx (ctx->prog is the program, ctx->idx the next instruction index; with ctx->image NULL the emit calls only advance the count). It sets is_main_prog = !bpf_is_subprog(prog), emits the KCFI hash for the main or subprog variant, notes idx0 = ctx->idx, then emits a BTI_JC landing pad, MOV x9, LR and a NOP. If prog->aux->exception_cb is false: it emits PACIASP when CONFIG_ARM64_PTR_AUTH_KERNEL is enabled, pushes FP and LR, sets FP = SP, calls prepare_bpf_tail_call_cnt, and if the program is not from cBPF and is a main program it computes cur_offset = ctx->idx - idx0 and, when that differs from PROLOGUE_OFFSET, prints pr_err_once and returns -1 immediately (ctx->idx stays at that point, ctx->stack_size is not yet set); otherwise in that case it emits a BTI_J pad; then it calls push_callee_regs. If exception_cb is true: it emits FP = x2 (the main program FP), SP = FP - 96, and sets ctx->fp_used = true. Then it sets ctx->stack_size = round_up(prog->aux->stack_depth, 16). If ctx->fp_used: with ctx->priv_sp_used it loads the private stack pointer (prog->aux->priv_stack_ptr + PRIV_STACK_GUARD_SZ plus the per-cpu offset) into the private-SP register and sets the BPF FP register to that plus ctx->stack_size, otherwise it sets the BPF FP register to SP. If ctx->stack_size is non-zero and ctx->priv_sp_used is false it emits SP = SP - ctx->stack_size. If ctx->arena_vm_start is non-zero it emits a load of that value into the arena base register. It then returns 0. The only return values are -1 (the PROLOGUE_OFFSET mismatch) and 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the FP/private-stack setup is guarded by ctx->fp_used (bpf_jit_comp.c slice 81-91) and the SP adjustment by stack_size and !priv_sp_used (94-95), while the old prose said they are done unconditionally. Slice cut the head; head read at bpf_jit_comp.c:511-535. Old statement that fp_used is set to true is only for the exception-callback case; kept.

name: csky_alignment
prose: Function csky_alignment(regs), the csky ABIv1 handler for a misaligned load/store fault; it returns nothing. It first picks the user or kernel path: for a user-mode fault it prints an error and goes to bad_area if align_usr_enable is zero, otherwise increments align_usr_count and reads the 16-bit instruction at the user instruction pointer with get_user, going to bad_area (after an error print) if that fails; for a kernel-mode fault it prints an error and goes to bad_area if align_kern_enable is zero, otherwise increments align_kern_count and reads the instruction directly. It then decodes rx (bits 3:0), imm (7:4), rz (11:8) and the opcode (bits 15:12); if rx or rz is 0 or 1 it goes to bad_area. For opcode OP_LDH, OP_LDW, OP_STH or OP_STW it computes addr = register rx + (imm << 1) for the halfword forms or + (imm << 2) for the word forms and calls ldh_c, ldw_c, sth_c or stw_c with rz and addr; for any other opcode the switch does nothing and ret is not assigned before the following test. If ret is non-zero it goes to bad_area; otherwise it advances regs->pc by 2 and returns. At bad_area: for a kernel-mode fault, if fixup_exception(regs) succeeds it returns; otherwise it prints the alert, shows the registers and calls make_task_dead(SIGKILL) (not expected to return). For a user-mode fault it calls force_sig_fault(SIGBUS, BUS_ADRALN, addr), where addr is 0 if bad_area was reached before an address was computed; regs->pc is not advanced.
note: The listed name do_alignment does not exist: slice cut the head and the real function is csky_alignment (abiv1/alignment.c:213). Fixed under the real name. Observation: ret is declared without an initialiser (line 214) and is only set by the four opcode cases (slice 9-26).

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, +)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic_fetch_add_relaxed(int i, atomic_t *v) (static __always_inline, produced by ATOMIC_FETCH_OP(add) inside ATOMIC_OPS(add, +); this definition is in the CONFIG_SMP branch of the header). It runs an inline-assembly load-exclusive/store-exclusive loop on v->counter: ldex.w loads the current value, the old value is copied to the return register, add i to the loaded value, stex.w stores it, and the loop repeats until the store-exclusive succeeds. It returns the value v->counter had before the successful update and leaves v->counter equal to that value plus i (32-bit addition). No barrier instruction is emitted other than the asm memory clobber (relaxed ordering), and no lock or reference is taken.
note: Macro-generated, atomic.h:49-60 (ATOMIC_FETCH_OP) and 76 (ATOMIC_OPS(add, +)). Name is the file-level invocation since the generated name does not occur literally.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, +)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic_add_return_relaxed(int i, atomic_t *v) (static __always_inline, produced by ATOMIC_OP_RETURN(add, +) inside ATOMIC_OPS(add, +); CONFIG_SMP branch). Its single statement returns arch_atomic_fetch_add_relaxed(i, v) + i. So v->counter is updated by that fetch-and-add LL/SC loop (relaxed ordering), and the return value is the value the counter held before the update plus i, the int sum computed after the update from the fetched old value; no lock or reference is taken.
note: Macro-generated, atomic.h:62-67 and 76. Old prose described the update correctly but not that the returned value is derived from the fetched old value rather than re-read.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(and)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic_fetch_and_relaxed(int i, atomic_t *v) (static __always_inline, produced by ATOMIC_FETCH_OP(and) inside the single-argument ATOMIC_OPS(and); CONFIG_SMP branch). It runs an inline-assembly load-exclusive/store-exclusive loop: ldex.w loads v->counter, the old value is kept for return, and the loaded value is ANDed with i and written back with stex.w, repeating until the store-exclusive succeeds. It returns the previous value of v->counter and leaves v->counter equal to previous AND i. Ordering is relaxed (only an asm memory clobber) and no lock or reference is taken.
note: Macro-generated, atomic.h:49-60 with the second ATOMIC_OPS definition and ATOMIC_OPS(and) at 91.

name: kprobe_ftrace_handler
prose: Ftrace callback for kprobes on csky, called with preemption disabled (stated by the comment on the function); arguments ip, parent_ip, ops and fregs, returns nothing. Returns and flow: (1) if kprobe_ftrace_disabled is set it returns immediately; (2) if ftrace_test_recursion_trylock(ip, parent_ip) returns a negative value it returns immediately; neither of these touches the recursion lock or per-cpu probe state. (3) Otherwise it holds the recursion lock until the single exit at the out label, where ftrace_test_recursion_unlock is called. It gets regs from fregs and looks up a kprobe at ip; if none, it looks up one at ip - MCOUNT_INSN_SIZE; if that lookup finds none, or the probe found there is disabled, it goes to out without changing anything else; if it found one there, it will use ip - MCOUNT_INSN_SIZE as the probe address (lr_saver). A probe found directly at ip is not checked for being disabled. (4) With probe p found, if kprobe_running() is true on this cpu it only calls kprobes_inc_nmissed_count(p), i.e. increments the missed count of the newly found probe p (not of the running one), leaves current_kprobe unchanged, and goes to out. (5) Otherwise it saves the current instruction pointer as orig_ip, sets the instruction pointer to ip (reduced when lr_saver), stores p in the per-cpu current_kprobe and sets the control block status to KPROBE_HIT_ACTIVE; if p has no pre_handler or the pre_handler returns 0, it sets the instruction pointer to p->addr + MCOUNT_INSN_SIZE, and if p has a post_handler it sets the status to KPROBE_HIT_SSDONE and calls it with the value 0, then restores the instruction pointer to orig_ip; if the pre_handler returns non-zero the post_handler is not called and the instruction pointer is left as the pre_handler set it. In every case of step (5) current_kprobe is then set to NULL before reaching out.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the missed count goes to p, the probe found for this ip, not to an already-running kprobe (ftrace.c slice line 33); old prose wrong. Round 2 (disabled check) is wrong about the prose: the prose already limited the disabled test to the ip - MCOUNT_INSN_SIZE probe, matching line 26. Original-rejection (current_kprobe not NULL on the missed and no-probe paths) is already what the old prose said (unchanged). Slice 6-63.

name: __CSKY_INSN_FUNCS(br16, 0xfc00, 0x0400)
prose: Generated function csky_insn_is_br16(probe_opcode_t code) (static __always_inline, returns bool; produced by __CSKY_INSN_FUNCS).
